title: The future seen from the past
subtitle: she would stay / I was going to say
summary: Talk about what was still in the future at a point in the past by using past forms of the verbs you would normally use for the future.

lesson.heading: How it works
lesson.text: To talk about an activity or event that was in the future at a particular point in the past, we use the past tenses of the verb forms we would normally use to talk about the future. These forms are very common in reporting.

examples.text: I haven't got much money, so I think **I'll stay** at home this summer.
Eleni decided that **she would stay** at home for the summer.

lesson.heading: The same forms, one step back
rows: **I'm not going to** say anything about the exams today.
**I wasn't going to** say anything about the exams, but the students asked me to.
**I'm having** a meeting with my tutor tomorrow.
I couldn't go to the match because **I was having** a meeting with my tutor.
**Will** you **be going** alone, or is Louise going with you?
At the time, I thought **I would be going** alone, but then Jan said he wanted to come.
The exam **will have finished** by three o'clock.
The exam was so easy that most people **would have finished** after 30 minutes.
**There is to be** a meeting of ministers this evening.
It was announced that **there was to be** a meeting of ministers that evening.
When the school closes, all the children **are to be** moved to one nearby.
Mrs Novak heard that **she was to be** moved to a post in a nearby school.
The bell **is about to** go, so pack your books away.
The bell **was about to** go when all the children started to pack their books away.

lesson.heading: Still in the future for the speaker
lesson.text: If the event seen from the past is still in the future for the speaker, either form is possible.

examples.text: It was announced this morning that there **is / was** to be a statement this evening.

left.label: It did happen
left.text: The rest of the sentence tells you.
examples: I didn't phone to give him the news because **we were seeing** each other later. He was very upset when I told him. (= we saw each other)

right.label: It didn't happen
right.text: The same form, the opposite outcome.
examples: **We were seeing** each other later that day, but I had to phone and cancel. (= we didn't see each other)

lesson.heading: was / were to + infinitive
lesson.text: We use was / were to + infinitive for something that was in the future at a point in the past and that actually happened.

examples.text: At the time she was probably the best actor in the theatre company, but in fact some of her colleagues **were to become** much better known.
He **was to find out** years later that the car he had bought was stolen.

lesson.heading: was / were to have + past participle
lesson.text: We use was / were to have + past participle for something that was expected but did not happen.

examples.text: The boat, which **was to have taken** them to the island, failed to arrive.
The meeting **was to have taken** place in the hall, but had to be cancelled at the last minute.

lesson.text: In less formal English, be supposed to sounds much more natural: *I was supposed to help, but I was ill.*

exercises.statement: When we were passing Ivan's house, we thought we'd drop in and see him.
exercises.explanation: Correct. Would (here 'd) is the past form of will, so it looks forward from a point in the past.

exercises.statement: I'm going to do the washing, but we'd run out of washing powder.
exercises.explanation: I was going to do the washing, but we'd run out of washing powder. The past context needs was going to.

exercises.statement: The concert tonight would be over by about 9:30. We could eat after that.
exercises.explanation: The concert tonight will be over by about 9:30. Tonight is still in the future for the speaker, so will is needed.

exercises.prompt: *A:* Where shall I hang my coat? *B:* Sorry, I thought Ella ___ you. Over there.
exercises.explanation: Would have + past participle is the past equivalent of will have + past participle.

exercises.prompt: The second half ___ to start, so shall we go back to our seats now?
exercises.explanation: 'Shall we go back now?' shows we are talking about the future from now, so the present form is right.

exercises.prompt: We didn't expect that having a rabbit as a pet ___ so many problems.
exercises.explanation: Reporting from a past point, so will becomes would.

exercises.prompt: Where's Oliver? He ___ to be here yesterday, and there's still no sign of him.
exercises.explanation: Yesterday is past, so the past form was supposed to is needed.

exercises.prompt: DNA testing ___ by police in the search for the missing Dublin schoolboy. His parents have welcomed the news.
exercises.explanation: The news is new and the testing is still ahead, so we look forward from now: is to be used.

exercises.prompt: Match each beginning with the ending that fits it.

pairs.left: The meeting was to have taken place in the hall, ...
pairs.right: ... but had to be cancelled at the last minute.

pairs.left: She was to have appeared with Heath Ledger in his last film, ...
pairs.right: ... but the part went to her sister.

pairs.left: Later, in Rome, I was to meet Professor Pearce, ...
pairs.right: ... and was very impressed by his knowledge of Italian culture.

pairs.left: The twenty police officers who were to have gone off duty at eight ...
pairs.right: ... had to remain in the police station.

pairs.left: It was to take 48 hours to get to Japan, ...
pairs.right: ... and we were exhausted when we arrived.

pairs.left: After the war he was to teach at London University ...

exercises.prompt: The construction of the cathedral was to have begun in 1650 ___
options: but a shortage of labour delayed the start for a further 20 years.
and go on for over 80 years.
exercises.explanation: Was to have + past participle says the expected event did not happen, so the ending must say why not.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to report an announcement made earlier that day.
exercises.answer: It was announced that there was to be a meeting of ministers that evening.
exercises.explanation: There is to be becomes there was to be when the announcement is reported from the past.

exercises.prompt: Did the event actually happen or not?

items.text: Some of her colleagues were to become much better known.
The boat, which was to have taken them to the island, failed to arrive.
He was to find out years later that the car he had bought was stolen.
I was supposed to help, but I was ill.
We were to stay with Rodrigo in Lisbon many times before he moved to Madrid.
The twenty police officers were to have gone off duty at eight.
